purpose: Define the Reader Edition literary style/layout contract independently of the 30 research parcels and independently of vendor-specific print dimensions.
transform: Keep title, author, frame, epigraph, body, and reader-aid roles semantically separate.
Preserve source wording, order, paragraph anchors, and source hash.
Keep verified reader aids visually distinct and subordinate.
Forbid reader aids from replacing or interrupting Irving's source paragraphs.
Defer trim size, margins, bleed, pagination, and other vendor-specific constraints to a later current-policy production gate.
proof: Tests protect source integrity and verified-only reader-aid admission.
Semantic roles can adapt without collapsing into one rigid style.
Vendor-specific layout is deliberately deferred, preserving the elastic production policy.
